roots.composeIntro: This Hub runs in a container, and the container itself cannot run the mount commands above the way the host can. Paste this block under the volumes: key of your docker-compose.yml, then the second block below attaches it to both the hub and worker services — the worker needs it too: when it leases a derive job it opens the source file itself, so mounting it into the Hub only makes every dispatched job end with “file not found”.
roots.composeNfsPreferred: Recommended route: an NFS volume mount needs no credentials and is the more secure of the two forms.
roots.composeNfsRecommended: NFS is preferred: if this NAS can export NFS shares, re-run this wizard with an NFS address (e.g. host:/export) — an NFS volume mount needs no credentials at all and avoids the problem below entirely.
roots.composeStep1: 1. Paste under the top-level volumes: of docker-compose.yml
roots.composeStep2: 2. Merge into services: — append that line to any service that already has volumes:
roots.composeStep3: 3. After docker compose up -d, the media folder to record is this path inside the container
roots.composeVerifyNote: On this route, fill in {path} when verifying in step 3 above — it is already the in-container path, so no translation is needed.
roots.containerPathNote: {hostPath} on the host is {containerPath} inside this container; the checks below apply to the latter.
roots.discoverIntro: Scan the LAN for NAS / SMB servers and find shares you can add directly. This is anonymous probing only; password-protected shares are flagged, and the mount password goes through the next wizard step, never through the browser.
roots.existsNotDir: {path} exists but is not a directory.
roots.guide.add-root: Add the mount point as a media folder
roots.guide.add-root-in-container: Back inside the Hub container — the host-side path is a different path in here, and the in-container one is the path to record
roots.guide.add-root-not-visible: This mount point is outside the directory bound into this container, so the Hub will never see it. Mount the share somewhere under the bound directory instead, then re-run this wizard — or rebuild the container with a bind that covers it.
roots.guide.compose-smb-cleartext: Docker’s local volume driver sends driver_opts straight to the mount(2) syscall and never runs the mount.cifs helper, so the credentials=/path/to/file form used elsewhere in this guide is rejected with "invalid argument" (docker/cli#2802, open since 2020-10-20). The password above has to be inline instead, which means it sits in cleartext in `docker volume inspect` output and in the volume’s opts.json under /var/lib/docker/volumes/. Every other secret in this project stays in an encrypted store that never reaches SQLite, an API response, or a log — this form is a documented fallback for when NFS is not available from the NAS, not the default. Note also the surface an operator is most likely to leak through: their own docker-compose.yml, which is a file that gets committed to git. Putting the password in ${NAS_PASSWORD} inside an untracked .env keeps it out of the repo, but does not save opts.json, because Docker stores the resolved value.
roots.guide.container-cannot-mount: This container cannot mount the share for itself, and that is deliberate: it runs as a fixed unprivileged user with no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and either that capability or a bind-mounted docker.sock would let it acquire the host mount authority it is specifically denied — docker.sock is the worse of the two, since it is unrestricted root on the Docker host, not merely on this container. That is why the steps above run on the Docker host instead of in here. If the share is mounted on the host after this container already started, it stays invisible inside the container unless the media bind carries "bind.propagation: rslave" in docker-compose.yml; without that, recreate the container (docker compose up -d) once the host mount exists.
roots.guide.container-run-on-host: Run the following on the machine hosting the Docker daemon — not inside this container
roots.guide.darwin-mount: Mount the share (the password is prompted for, not typed here)
roots.guide.fstab: Make it survive a reboot — append to /etc/fstab
roots.guide.read-only: The mount is read-only on purpose. Footage is never written to, and a read-only mount makes that true of the whole share rather than only of this program.
roots.guide.smb-credentials-file: Put the credentials in a file only root can read
roots.guide.staging-copy: Set "source_staging": {"mode": "copy"} in config.json for a network media folder. FFmpeg reading a 4K source over SMB for every derive is what makes a NAS library crawl; copy mode stages the file into cache/sources/ once instead.
roots.guide.windows-service-drive-letter: A drive letter mapped in your own session does not exist for a service running as another account. If the Hub runs as a service, give it the UNC path (\\host\share\folder) instead of the letter.
roots.guide.worker-same-path: A Worker needs the same footage at the same path, or an explicit --mount root-id=/its/own/path when it enrols.
roots.guide.wsl-namespace: Under WSL2 a mount made in an interactive shell is invisible to systemd services and to other SSH sessions, because they are in different mount namespaces. The nsenter prefix above mounts into PID 1’s namespace, where everything can see it.
roots.guide.wsl-not-persistent: WSL2 does not persist mounts across a restart of the distribution. Either re-run the mount command, or add it to the boot command in /etc/wsl.conf.

settings.cooldownHint: Forced seconds of waiting after each job completes. This is the switch that turns “hours of continuous saturation” into “intermittent load”; limiting speed alone still keeps the disk reading. 0 means no wait; the cap is 3600.
settings.costHint.lead: Cloud calls (analysis, transcription) are estimated per entry into the ledger using the provider’s billing info; here you set the daily / monthly cost reference values. The reference only helps you observe cost — it never limits or defers cloud calls, and the ledger is an append-only, post-hoc estimate, never a bill. Units match the provider’s billing info (per request / per minute of video / per minute of audio).
settings.dailyCostHint.lead: Estimated reference for the current day (UTC), for comparison only; reaching or exceeding it does not block analysis / transcription.
settings.deferAboveHint.lead: Footage larger than this is processed only within the window; everything else runs anytime.
settings.deferAboveHint.tail: . The decision uses size, not duration, because what the disk feels is how many bytes were read. Deferred jobs are never started, so they consume no retries.
settings.diskProtectionHint: The pipeline writes its outputs (thumbnails, preview videos, audio extracts) to the Hub’s cache disk. When the cache disk fills up, FFmpeg reports “disk full” mid-encode — those failures are now recognized and the job is deferred rather than retried in place and burning retries; the setting below makes jobs check free space before they start.
settings.enableOffPeakHint: When off, deferred jobs are released immediately instead of being held.
settings.immediateBelowHint: Footage under this size is exempt from both deferral and speed limiting. Phone clips cost almost nothing to generate; throttling them only makes the library look broken without saving anything. Must be below the threshold above.
settings.intro: Changes apply immediately; no Hub restart needed — the pipeline re-reads the limits before every run, and tasks already in flight are constrained right away.
settings.loadHint: Jobs run one at a time, so this is not about how many run at once. A single transcode process reading a 4K file at full speed can saturate a mechanical drive or a NAS link, and a full-library scan can run for hours — the real levers are read speed and the pause between jobs. Both are off by default.
settings.minFreeSpaceHint.lead: When the cache disk’s free space drops below this, heavy jobs (generation, transcription, analysis) do not start; they are deferred for low disk space and retried automatically after 10 minutes without consuming a retry.
settings.minFreeSpaceHint.tail: . A disk-full failure itself is deferred the same way whether or not this is enabled.
settings.monthlyCostHint.lead: Estimated reference for the current month (UTC), for comparison only; reaching or exceeding it does not block jobs.
settings.offPeakHint.tail: . Within the window, waiting is unlimited (there is nothing to protect at night — finishing at full speed is the point). An end time earlier than the start time means it crosses midnight, e.g. 22:00–06:00.
settings.offPeakWindowHint: Includes the start time, excludes the end time.
settings.readRateHint.lead: The cap on how fast source files are read, in “real-time multiples”: 1 means a 10-minute clip takes 10 minutes to read.
settings.readRateHint.tail: . Only whole-file reads (proxy, audio extraction) honor it; a thumbnail decodes a single frame, so limiting it only slows seeking. The floor is 0.25.
settings.saved: Saved; takes effect on the next job.

Everything else lives on the Hub’s cache disk: preview videos, thumbnails, and audio can all be regenerated from the source footage,
settings.storageHint.tail: ; temporary files can be removed anytime.
